accessor.callers_in_window: called once at 0x514f8f8 with rdi = the snapshot object
accessor.negative_arm_note: the js arm at 0x514f900 jumps to the unsigned-to-double conversion at 0x514fca0; it is unreachable for the accessor's own range (a saturating difference is never negative as a signed value unless the difference exceeds 2^63, which the conversion handles), and the model uses a plain unsigned-to-double conversion covering both arms
accessor.rule: returns max(0, [rdi+0x130] - [rdi+0x128]) as an unsigned 64-bit value: the difference is computed, then the zero is selected when [rdi+0x128] >= [rdi+0x130] (cmovae after cmp %rdx,%rcx)

bounded_question: What does node #94 function 0x514f770 render from a snapshot object, which fields feed each line, and how are the saturating window, the clock chain and the per-entry ratios computed?

caller_census.method: full .text e8 scan, e9 scan, whole-file qword scan
caller_census.note: callers are census only; their argument objects are not modelled here (the 0x514fd60 enclosing function is the same one that calls the timed-snapshot refresh at 0x514fda5)

cleanup.fde: none of its own; covered by the window FDE's LSDA
cleanup.note: the exception cleanup block sits immediately BEFORE the window (not in its own FDE): it disposes the rsp+0x40 temp string, the rbp temp string and the r14 ostringstream, then checks the canary and calls _Unwind_Resume. The window's own tail stubs (0x514fcf4, 0x514fd00, 0x514fd0c, 0x514fd18, 0x514fd24) jump into its staged entries; which stub serves which call site is not claimed (LSDA mapping)

clock_chain.rule: node 0: inner = [holder], slot = [inner+0x98]; if slot != sentinel cell, call slot with rdi = holder. Node 1: wrapper = [holder+0x20], inner = [wrapper], slot = [inner+0x98]; if slot != node 0 slot value, call slot with rdi = wrapper. Node 2: wrapper = [previous wrapper+0x20], inner = [wrapper], call [inner+0x98] unconditionally with rdi = wrapper. A chain that runs out of nodes before the unconditional call would dereference a null link; the model raises ChainExhausted
clock_chain.shared_note: the sentinel cell 0x5777bc8 and the +0x98 slot are shared with the timed-snapshot clock chain (RE-001-timed-snapshot-94), but this walk is a distinct 3-node walk with +0x20 wrapper links, not the 4-node walk there

composed_rule: the window renders one BlockCache report into the destination string: a header line naming the snapshot identity and its capacity, usage, table size, occupancy, collection counters, last_secs ratio and secs_since value, then an entry-stats section listing every nonzero entry with its count, scaled size and portion ratio, terminated by a newline
the snapshot object is 0x138 bytes and shares its layout with the timed-snapshot packet: +0x120/+0x124 counters, +0x128 raw clock value, +0x130 commit value, +0x20 identity string

last_secs is the saturating accessor window (commit minus snapshot clock, floored at zero) divided by 1,000,000.0 as a double; secs_since is the fresh clock-chain value minus the commit value, divided by 1,000,000 as an unsigned integer via the magic multiply

each entry ratio is its value times 100.0 divided by the snapshot+0x00 field, as doubles; the entry names come from the runtime-populated .bss table at 0x578c2e0 and are parameters to the model, not claims from the binary

secs_since_magic.verified: checked against integer //1000000 for 0, 1, 999, 1000, 10^12, 2^64-1 and 2000 random 64-bit values; equals floor division by 1,000,000, the same divisor as last_secs

name_table.note: the table lives in .bss, so its entries are populated at runtime and are NOT retained in the binary; the model takes the 14 names as parameters and claims nothing about their runtime contents
name_table.record_layout: pointer at record+0x00, length at record+0x08; remaining 16 bytes unused by this function

per_entry.field: name string from the table record (pointer, length)
counter at snapshot+0xb0 + i*8 as unsigned decimal

per_entry.helper: 0x5430570 on the value at snapshot+0x40 + i*8

per_entry.computed: ratio = (value * 100.0) / snapshot+0x00, both operands converted as unsigned 64-bit values (js arms at 0x514fc60 and 0x514fc80 handle the sign-bit case), inserted with default ostream formatting; a zero denominator yields inf (nan when the value is also zero), as in C++ double division

entry_loop.skip_rule: an entry whose counter is zero is skipped entirely (no name, no separators)

header_sequence.computed: accessor 0x514df50(snapshot) as a double divided by 1,000,000.0 (double at 0x20ae60), inserted with default ostream formatting
(clock_chain_value - snapshot+0x130) divided by 1,000,000 with the unsigned magic multiply (constant 0x431bde82d7b634db, shift 18 after the 128-bit multiply), inserted as unsigned decimal

helper.arguments: rdi = destination string, rsi = value (signed entry with a js arm at 0x5430680 that converts it as unsigned, so the model treats the input as an unsigned 64-bit value)
helper.rule: value is converted to a double, multiplied by 1/1024 (double at 0x20a600), and while the scaled value is >= 1024.0 (double at 0x20aeb8) it is multiplied by 1/1024 again, stepping the unit KB -> MB -> GB -> TB (TB is terminal, no further compare). The result is formatted with snprintf format '%.2f %s' (at 0x1de3ae) using unit strings 'KB' (0x1ea2c0), 'MB' (0x1e5f2d), 'GB' (0x1e4a27), 'TB' (0x1e920c)
helper.scope_note: bound here as a callee only; the full 500-byte helper body is excerpted verbatim, but this item does not re-claim its internal string handling

fields.+0x00: 8-byte value, formatted by helper 0x5430570 as capacity, and used as the denominator of every per-entry ratio
fields.+0x08: 8-byte value, formatted by helper 0x5430570 as usage
fields.+0x120: 32-bit counter, inserted as collections (read as 32-bit mov)
fields.+0x124: 32-bit counter, inserted as last_copies (read as 32-bit mov)
fields.+0x128: raw clock value stored at snapshot build time (see the RE-001-timed-snapshot-94 correction: the builder receives the raw clock value in rcx, not the elapsed value)
fields.+0x130: commit-time clock value, used by the accessor and by the secs_since subtraction
fields.+0x20: identity string object (pointer at +0x20, length at +0x28), inserted after 'Block cache '
fields.+0x40: 14 x 8-byte values, one per entry, formatted by helper 0x5430570 (entry index i at +0x40 + i*8)
fields.+0xb0: 14 x 8-byte counters, one per entry (entry index i at +0xb0 + i*8); a zero counter skips its entry

unknowns: the identities of the snapshot, clock-holder and wrapper objects and what the report means to its readers
the clock values' time unit (the labels say secs, but the divisor 1,000,000 (and 1,000,000.0 for last_secs) does not pin a unit from the bytes alone)
the runtime contents of the .bss entry-name table and of the sentinel cell 0x5777bc8
which landing stub serves which call site (LSDA mapping not claimed)
the reaching path: the two direct callers are census only

arguments.rdi: destination string (saved at rsp+0x18; the rendered report is assigned into it at the end; the function returns void)
